claim_verdicts.evidence: Redis FAQ: "Redis is an in-memory but persistent on disk database"; "Redis is an acronym that stands for REmote DIctionary Server." Data-store quick start: "You can use the same data types as in your local programming environment but on the server side within Redis." Execution: a key set from the lab box (review:probe) was read back by a separate redis-cli invocation; donhang-redis is its own container (redis:8.10.2-alpine).

Definitional (glossary term key-value-store). Consistent with Redis data-store quick start: "Store data under a key in Redis", "Retrieve data with a key from Redis"; the lesson restricts itself to SET/GET on strings, where no table or JOIN exists.

Engine networking, Published ports: ports on bridge networks "are not accessible from outside the host"; "Use the --publish or -p flag to make a port available outside the host". docker-compose.yml:112 @ stage-2: ConnectionStrings__Redis: "redis:6379,abortConnect=false". StackExchange.Redis Configuration: "Tokens in the configuration string are comma-separated; any without an = sign are assumed to be redis server endpoints"; abortConnect={bool} is a client option (AbortOnConnectFail) - backs section 5 "The rest of that setting is an option for the Redis client inside the API." Execution: redis-cli -h redis INFO server -> tcp_port:6379.

SET: syntax "SET key value [...] [EX seconds | ...]"; "EX seconds: Set the specified expire time, in seconds (a positive integer)." Example: SET anotherkey "will expire in a minute" EX 60 -> OK. Execution: SET product:3 ... EX 60 -> OK, TTL -> 60.

TTL: "Returns the remaining time to live of a key that has a timeout." Return information: "TTL in seconds"; "-1 if the key exists but has no associated expiration"; "-2 if the key does not exist." Execution: TTL after expiry -> -2.

EXPIRE: "Set a timeout on key. After the timeout has expired, the key will automatically be deleted." Appendix: "When a key has an expire set, Redis will make sure to remove the key when the specified amount of time elapsed." (Physically: passive on access, or active random sampling.) Execution: after EX 2 + sleep 3, TTL -2 and GET printed an empty line.

SET: "If key already holds a value, it is overwritten, regardless of its type. Any previous time to live associated with the key is discarded on successful SET operation." EXPIRE: "The timeout will only be cleared by commands that delete or overwrite the contents of the key, including DEL, SET". Execution: SET t:x 1 EX 100; SET t:x 2; TTL t:x -> -1.

Strings: "Redis strings store sequences of bytes, including text, serialized objects, and binary arrays." "Values can be strings (including binary data) of every kind". Execution: redis-cli -h redis SET product:9 '{"priceVnd":-5}' EX 5 -> OK.

Redis FAQ: "Redis is an in-memory but persistent on disk database, so it represents a different trade off where very high write and read speed is achieved with the limitation of data sets that can't be larger than memory." Also: "data served from memory, disk used for storage."

issues.text: The later-setup wording is now clear, but this sentence carries three ideas and I re-read it: 'it' in 'restarting the API empties it' could be the Dictionary or the API's memory.
